target_profile.system_boundary: The library package raft of github.com/hashicorp/raft, built per instance as one Raft object that owns its own persistent state (currentTerm, last vote, log, snapshots) and its own main-thread state machine (Follower/Candidate/Leader). Distributed behaviour emerges only from N Raft instances exchanging RPCs through an injected Transport; the FSM, LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and Transport are caller-supplied.
protocol_contexts: multi-server static voter set bootstrapped from a configuration
cluster with non-voting servers (nonvoters eligible for log replication but not votes)
cluster undergoing a configuration change (one uncommitted configuration at a time)
external_interfaces: Transport (AppendEntries, RequestVote, RequestPreVote, InstallSnapshot, TimeoutNow, Consumer)
ownership: each Raft instance owns its persistent term, vote, log and snapshot; no shared store is assumed
the leader main thread owns the commitment object, the inflight logFuture list and one followerReplication per peer
a separate FSM goroutine owns application of committed entries to the caller FSM
selection_injection: FSM, LogStore, StableStore and SnapshotStore are always injected by the caller; Transport is injected as well, but the library also ships its own NetworkTransport, TCPTransport and InmemTransport implementations, so socket and connection handling is library code whenever those are used
variants: ProtocolVersion 2 vs 3 (legacy peers/config entries vs ID-based configuration)
pre-vote enabled (transport implements WithPreVote) vs disabled
unknowns: Wiring and fault assumptions of the concrete caller FSM and durable stores are outside the library; their correctness is not established here.

The in-repo Transport implementations (net_transport.go, tcp_transport.go, inmem_transport.go) were not read in this run; their framing, connection lifecycle, heartbeat fast-path dispatch, pipeline ordering and in-process delivery behaviour remain unmapped library responsibilities.

activities.purpose: Form a decision (leader election / log agreement) and advance the replicated log legally.
activities.realization_summary: The leader main thread appends entries to its LogStore, dispatches them onto inflight futures, and a per-peer replication goroutine copies entries to followers via AppendEntries; the commitment object aggregates per-voter durable match indexes and advances the leader commit index once a quorum matches at or beyond the term's startIndex, after which the leader hands committed entries to the FSM goroutine.

activities.purpose: Acquire, transfer or lose authority and keep the term/leader context valid.
activities.realization_summary: A follower that times out starts a candidate loop; a campaign (optionally pre-vote) raises currentTerm, persists a self-vote and tallies RequestVote responses up to a majority. Followers adopt a leader identity and raise their term on AppendEntries/RequestVote/InstallSnapshot, and a leader steps down on a newer term or when its lease quorum lapses.

activities.purpose: Recover and resynchronize an eligible participant that has fallen behind the log.
activities.realization_summary: An InstallSnapshot RPC lets a leader ship a full snapshot to a lagging follower, which spills it to a local SnapshotStore, restores the FSM, moves lastApplied/lastSnapshot and adopts the snapshot's configuration. At startup an instance restores the newest usable local snapshot before scanning configuration entries.

activities.purpose: Maintain configuration and participant eligibility as an authoritative replicated decision.
activities.realization_summary: AddVoter/AddNonvoter/RemoveServer/DemoteVoter enqueue a configurationChangeRequest that the leader turns into a single configuration log entry (or a legacy peer entry for protocol < 2); the entry is committed like any other and, once committed, the committed configuration changes voter eligibility. Latest and committed configuration indexes are tracked separately.

activities.purpose: Apply committed decisions to the caller FSM and report completion.
activities.realization_summary: The FSM goroutine receives batches of commitTuple on fsmMutateCh and calls FSM.Apply (or ApplyBatch), or ingests a restored snapshot; it responds to the associated logFuture with the FSM result and tracks lastIndex/lastTerm.

activities.purpose: Persist and reconstruct the history that supports decisions.
activities.realization_summary: Term, last vote, log entries, configuration indexes and snapshots are written to caller-supplied durable stores; setCurrentTerm persists before updating memory, persistence of a vote is a precondition of granting it, and log compaction/snapshots bound log growth.

activities.purpose: Expose the invocation interval and observed completion of client operations.
activities.realization_summary: Client calls enqueue a logFuture/verifyFuture on a channel; the returned Future is completed when the leader applies the entry, when leadership is lost (ErrLeadershipLost), or on timeout/shutdown. The library owns the future contract; the caller owns when to call and how to interpret results.

facts.meaning: The monotonic term this instance currently believes it is in; used as the fence for every vote, entry acceptance and authority decision.
facts.validity_context: valid from the moment the durable write succeeds until replaced by a strictly greater term; survives restart because it is read back in NewRaft.
facts.durability: written to the caller StableStore before the in-memory value changes.
facts.recovery: NewRaft reads CurrentTerm from StableStore at start.

facts.meaning: The single candidate this instance has voted for within the current term, the safety record that prevents a second vote in the same term after a restart.
facts.validity_context: valid for the term recorded alongside it; replaced when a later term is voted in.
facts.durability: persistVote writes both keys; a grant is only answered after a successful persist.
facts.recovery: Read back by requestVote on subsequent requests.

facts.meaning: A replicated log entry identified by (index, term, type, data) that carries client commands, barriers, no-ops and configuration changes.
facts.validity_context: valid as written; a leader may overwrite a follower's suffix at the same index with a different term during conflict resolution.
facts.durability: leader and follower both call LogStore.StoreLogs; conflicting suffixes are deleted with DeleteRange.
facts.recovery: lastIndex/lastLog are read from LogStore in NewRaft and replayed from the last snapshot.

facts.meaning: The highest log index this instance treats as committed: on a leader, a quorum durable match at or beyond the term's startIndex; on a follower, min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex).
facts.validity_context: monotonic within an instance; a follower's value is derived from the current leader's advertised LeaderCommitIndex.
facts.durability: not itself persisted; recomputed from the log and configuration, but bounded by startIndex while a leader.
facts.recovery: after restart the commit index is re-derived as entries are re-applied or re-advertised by a leader.

facts.meaning: The highest log index the caller FSM has ingested, either through Apply/ApplyBatch or through a Restore of a snapshot.
facts.validity_context: advances only after the FSM has consumed the entry; used to decide what to replay after restart.
facts.durability: held by the caller FSM; the Raft library only remembers lastSnapshot durably.
facts.recovery: on start, the snapshot index becomes lastApplied and later log entries are re-applied.

facts.meaning: The leader address and ID this instance currently attributes authority to, advertised to clients and used to reject conflicting vote requests.
facts.validity_context: cleared on every state transition and re-established when a claiming leader's RPC is accepted.
facts.durability: not durable; reconstructed after restart from the first accepted RPC from a leader.
facts.recovery: unknown after restart until a leader contacts the instance.

facts.meaning: The cluster configuration (servers, suffrage) as latest and as committed, each with the log index of its configuration entry.

identity.component: latest and committed Configuration with their indexes

facts.validity_context: latest configuration may be uncommitted; committed configuration is the one whose entry is committed and is what determines current voter eligibility.
facts.durability: encoded in configuration log entries and in snapshot metadata.
facts.recovery: NewRaft scans log entries after the last snapshot to rebuild the latest/committed configuration.

facts.meaning: A durable snapshot of the FSM at a given index/term together with the configuration in force at that index.
facts.validity_context: valid once Persist has committed it and it is listed by the SnapshotStore; older snapshots may be removed.
facts.durability: written by the SnapshotStore implementation; the library tracks only the index/term of the newest snapshot.
facts.recovery: restoreSnapshot at startup and installSnapshot at runtime both rebuild state from it.

facts.meaning: The instance's in-memory claim of the last durable log coordinate it holds: lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm together with lastSnapshotIndex/lastSnapshotTerm, surfaced through getLastLog, getLastEntry and getLastIndex. It is the value a follower returns as AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog, the value it compares an incoming previous-log coordinate against, and the last-log coordinate a candidate advertises when soliciting votes.
facts.validity_context: Valid only while it describes the log and snapshot the instance actually holds. Appending raises the log part; a conflict truncation replaces it; installSnapshot and snapshot compaction can remove the entries an older value named. It is not persisted: NewRaft derives the log part from LogStore.LastIndex and the snapshot part from the stable store, so a restart recomputes it from durable state. Two confirmed in-scope violations are runtime failures of this condition: after a conflict truncation whose replacement StoreLogs fails the log part keeps the deleted indices (check 25473e1b731e4c2692e47975fef6d3a0), and after installSnapshot clears a monotonic log store the log part keeps the pre-install index instead of the installed snapshot index (check 58ebdb2f92184614b01ecfab56fe2bc9).
facts.durability: In-memory only. A restart rebuilds it from the LogStore and SnapshotStore, which is why a runtime transition that leaves it stale is repaired only by restart.
facts.recovery: Recomputed at construction; no handler is required to re-derive it at runtime, so each runtime transition that changes the durable log must keep it consistent itself.
unknowns: Reachability of the installSnapshot case from a legal leader history remains open: the confirmed witness needs a follower whose watermark index exceeds the leader's snapshot index (check 58ebdb2f92184614b01ecfab56fe2bc9).

For the truncation-failure case while the leader still holds the log, the follower is left unrepaired short of a restart (see this Fact's validity_context); the open variant is the one where the leader's own log has been compacted below the failure point, which routes replication into the snapshot path and interacts with the installSnapshot finding.

The library sequences and batches entries but deterministic application and snapshot state are the caller FSM's contract.

formation.explanation: A decision is formed as a log entry and advanced only after a quorum has durably stored it. The leader's dispatchLogs assigns (index, term) to each logFuture, stores it locally and records its own match; each peer's followerReplication goroutine copies entries with AppendEntries and, on success, records that peer's durable match index through commitment.match. commitment.recalculate sorts the voter match indexes, takes the quorum-position match and advances commitIndex only when it is both above the current value and at or beyond the term's startIndex. leaderLoop consumes commitCh, moves the inflight prefix up to the commit index and hands it to the FSM goroutine. A follower mirrors this by clamping its commit index to min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex) and applying the same logs.

context.explanation: Authority is a per-instance, durable term plus at most one vote. A follower that stops hearing from a leader starts a candidate loop that raises currentTerm (persisted first) and solicits votes, optionally behind a non-mutating pre-vote. A vote is granted only to a candidate in the configuration whose log is at least as up to date, and only after the vote is persisted, so the same term cannot vote twice even across restart. Any RPC carrying a higher term forces the receiver to Follower and adopts the sender's term and, for leader RPCs, the sender's leader identity. A leader keeps authority while a quorum of voters is in recent contact and abandons it on a newer term, a failed verification, or a lapsed lease.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the term fence carried by every entry. A log entry is only meaningful together with the term of the leader that wrote it: a follower accepts new entries only when the previous-log coordinate matches its own log and only after adopting a term that is not older, and a new leader may not commit an entry from an earlier term merely because it is stored on a majority — commitment.startIndex forces the current term's opening no-op (or an equivalent entry) to be committed first. Conversely, authority transitions constrain which pending support may still be consumed: when a leader steps down it answers every inflight logFuture and pending verifyFuture with ErrLeadershipLost, and a follower that truncates a conflicting suffix also rolls its latest configuration back to the committed one, so an uncommitted configuration cannot survive on a minority that lost the election.

open_details: Pipeline mode (pipelineReplicate/pipelineSend/pipelineDecode) was read only at the level needed to see how a peer match is recorded; its internal response ordering was not traced in full.

Leadership transfer (leadershipTransfer/initiateLeadershipTransfer) was read at the level of the TimeoutNow path and the leader-side timeout handling; the interaction between a transfer and a concurrent configuration change was not traced.
restoreUserSnapshot (external snapshot restore) was read but its interaction with an in-flight configuration entry was not traced end to end.
core_overview.rationale: Both core lines are grounded in read, cited implementation: decision formation and legal advancement through dispatch -> replication -> commitment -> leaderLoop, and authority/term context through the candidate loop, vote persistence and term/leader adoption. Their connection is concrete: the term fence on each entry, the startIndex restriction on committing prior-term entries, the ErrLeadershipLost sweep of pending futures on step-down, and the configuration rollback on suffix truncation. Local details (pipeline internals, leadership transfer interaction, external snapshot restore) remain open but do not break the backbone.
